title: Implement draft-ietf-jmap-conditional-02 (conditional/atomic Foo/set, opt-in registration)
description: draft-ietf-jmap-conditional-02 (WG draft, posted 2026-10-26; successor of draft-gondwana-jmap-conditional-00) adds capability urn:ietf:params:jmap:conditional: preconditions on any Foo/set (section 3, stateMismatch SetError), atomic Foo/set (section 4, atomicFailure and cannotApplyAtomically method errors), with FileNode force-with-lease, conditional destroy and atomic rename/replace examples (section 5). Implementations: Cyrus, Fastmail. crate-jmap has no implementation: no conditional symbols; the generic /set path is in crate-jmap-server. Like emailpush and blobext (JMAP-r44n, JMAP-tna1): do only if wanted. If not wanted, close as N/A, no crate. If wanted: types (capability and error codes) in crate-jmap-types, evaluation and atomic apply in the crate-jmap-server set path with a backend hook for atomicity, client builders in crate-jmap-base-client. Source: /data/PROJECT/IETF/specs/draft-ietf-jmap-conditional-02.{txt,xml} (downloaded 2026-11-12).
notes:
Decision Mark 2026-11-12: crate-jmap aims to be THE complete reference implementation covering the JMAP specs, so this is required work, not optional. Split rule: the crates own wire types, validation, method semantics and error mapping; storage-, transport- or media-specific work is pushed to the calling crate through backend trait hooks (see the spec-method-defaults memory: no no-op default when that would put wrong data on the wire). Here: precondition evaluation, stateMismatch, atomicFailure and the capability live in crate-jmap-types/crate-jmap-server, applied to every /set (including the per-family servers); atomic apply goes through a backend hook, and a backend that cannot apply atomically returns cannotApplyAtomically (section 4.3). Client builders in crate-jmap-base-client. Split into children when work starts.
